metadata.primary_principle: Scientific KB + personal baseline + age/life-stage + lifestyle + current observation; general model knowledge is fallback hypothesis only.
metadata.current_intent_taxonomy: Use repository IntentCode from backend/app/contracts/taxonomy.py as source of truth.

source_registry.citation: Siniscalchi M. et al. (2018). Communication in Dogs. Animals, 8(8), 131.
source_registry.use: Core review for visual, acoustic, tactile and olfactory canine communication; context dependence.

source_registry.citation: Waller B.M. et al. (2013). Paedomorphic Facial Expressions Give Dogs a Selective Advantage. PLOS ONE 8(12):e82686.
source_registry.use: DogFACS development; anatomically grounded facial movement coding. Use movements as observables, not emotion labels.

source_registry.citation: Kaminski J. et al. (2017). Human attention affects facial expressions in domestic dogs. Scientific Reports.
source_registry.use: Facial movements are affected by human attention; warning against context-free emotion reading.

source_registry.citation: Caeiro C.C. et al. (2017). Dogs and humans respond to emotionally competent stimuli by producing different facial actions. Scientific Reports.
source_registry.use: Distinct facial-action patterns across experimental contexts; supports feature-level coding.

source_registry.citation: Bremhorst A. et al. (2022). Evaluating the accuracy of facial expressions as emotion indicators across contexts in dogs. Animal Cognition.
source_registry.use: Facial indicators can fail to generalize across contexts; reinforces abstention and context weighting.

source_registry.citation: Bremhorst A. et al. (2023). Explainable automated recognition of emotional states from canine facial expressions. Scientific Reports.
source_registry.use: Controlled-state automated classification evidence; narrow population/context, not universal emotion decoder.

source_registry.citation: Martvel G. et al. (2025). Dog facial landmarks detection and its applications for facial analysis. Scientific Reports 15, 21886.
source_registry.use: DogFLW landmarks and DogFACS-related facial analysis; dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0.

source_registry.citation: Morrill K. et al. (2022). Ancestry-inclusive dog genomics challenges popular breed stereotypes. Science 376:eabk0639.
source_registry.use: Breed explains about 9% of individual behavioral variation; breed is a weak prior, not a behavioral verdict.

source_registry.citation: Mellor-related state-of-the-art review: Where Do We Stand in the Domestic Dog Positive-Emotion Assessment? Frontiers in Psychology (2020).
source_registry.use: Positive/negative affect indicators overlap; individual variability and multimodal assessment are essential.

source_registry.citation: AAHA Canine and Feline Behavior Management Guidelines — Common Signs of Anxiety/Distress.
source_registry.use: Clinical list of nonspecific anxiety/distress signs; use for safety escalation, not diagnosis.

source_registry.citation: Mota-Rojas D. et al. (2021). Current Advances in Assessment of Dog’s Emotions, Facial Expressions, and Their Use for Clinical Recognition of Pain. Animals 11, 3334.
source_registry.use: Pain-related behavioral/facial changes exist but no single facial trait is diagnostic; combine signals and history.

source_registry.citation: AAHA/AAFP Pain Management Guidelines for Dogs and Cats.
source_registry.use: Behavioral change is central to pain assessment; validated scales and veterinary evaluation required.

source_registry.citation: Brady K. et al. (2018). Systematic Review of Reliability and Validity of Behavioural Tests in Working Dogs. Frontiers in Veterinary Science 5:103.
source_registry.use: Behavior tests vary in reliability/validity; test context and repeatability matter.

source_registry.citation: Methods of behavioral testing in dogs: a scoping review and analysis of test stimuli. Frontiers in Veterinary Science (2024).
source_registry.use: 392 publications / 2,362 tests; supports standardized context taxonomy and low-stress testing.

source_registry.citation: Yin S., McCowan B. (2004). Barking in domestic dogs: context specificity and individual identification. Animal Behaviour.
source_registry.use: Barks differ acoustically by context and individual; context classification is probabilistic.

source_registry.citation: Faragó T. et al. (2017). Dog growls express various contextual and affective content for human listeners. Royal Society Open Science.
source_registry.use: Growls vary by social context; human interpretation is above chance but imperfect.

source_registry.citation: Abzaliev A., Pérez-Espinosa H., Mihalcea R. (2024). Towards Dog Bark Decoding: Leveraging Human Speech Processing for Automated Bark Classification. LREC-COLING.
source_registry.use: Human speech embeddings support dog bark classification for individual, breed, sex and context; limited dataset.

source_registry.citation: University of Michigan Engineering (2024). Using AI to decode dog vocalizations.
source_registry.use: Accessible summary of 74-dog dataset and up-to-70% classification results.

source_registry.citation: Google AudioSet — Dog/Bark ontology and dataset.
source_registry.use: Large weakly contextual audio-event corpus; dataset CC BY 4.0, ontology CC BY-SA 4.0. Good for bark/noise detection, not intent labels.

source_registry.citation: DogSpeak Dataset (ACM MM 2025 release / Hugging Face).
source_registry.use: Large canine vocalization corpus for representation learning; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, therefore not suitable for commercial training without separate permission.

source_registry.citation: Canine Age Transition Vocalization Dataset (Hugging Face).
source_registry.use: Longitudinal bark units with age/breed metadata; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, research/benchmark only unless relicensed.

source_registry.citation: BORIS — Behavioral Observation Research Interactive Software.
source_registry.use: Open-source GPLv3 annotation/logging tool; suitable annotation workflow utility.

source_registry.citation: WSAVA Global Nutrition Guidelines and Toolkit.
source_registry.use: Nutrition assessment must be individualized and tied to veterinary context; supports data model for diet history and body condition.

source_registry.citation: Consistency of faecal scoring using two canine faecal scoring systems (2021). Journal of Small Animal Practice.
source_registry.use: Fecal scoring has inter-observer variability; image model should expose uncertainty and trend, not false precision.

source_registry.citation: WSAVA/ENOVAT Canine Acute Diarrhea Treatment Summary (2025).
source_registry.use: Systemic clinical signs matter more than stool appearance alone for severity; supports escalation logic.

source_registry.citation: AAHA — Help! Is This a Pet Emergency? (2024).
source_registry.use: Emergency red flags for persistent vomiting/diarrhea, breathing difficulty, collapse, severe weakness, sudden behavior change.

source_registry.citation: AAHA (2026). Why is my Dog throwing up? Vets explain when it's serious.
source_registry.use: GI red flags: repeated vomiting, inability to keep water down, blood, black/tarry stool, lethargy/collapse, painful/bloated abdomen.

source_registry.citation: AAHA (2019). Canine Life Stage Definitions / 2019 Canine Life Stage Guidelines.
source_registry.use: Life stage should be individualized by age, size, lifestyle, health status and breed; stages phase in/out rather than changing abruptly.

source_registry.citation: AAHA (2019). Behavior — Canine Life Stage Guidelines.
source_registry.use: Behavioral recommendations vary across puppy, young/mature adult and senior stages; individual exercise/cognitive engagement and monitoring of change are emphasized.

source_registry.citation: AAHA (2019). Life Stage Checklists.
source_registry.use: Lifestyle, exercise, mental stimulation and enrichment should be appropriate to age, breed and temperament; senior dogs require environmental and cognitive monitoring.

source_registry.citation: AVSAB (2024 revision). Puppy Socialization Position Statement.
source_registry.use: Early socialization is important, must be positive, safe and not forced; fearful puppies warrant veterinary guidance.

source_registry.citation: AVSAB (2021). Humane Dog Training Position Statement.
source_registry.use: Reward-based methods are recommended; aversive methods should not be used as standard training/behavior modification advice.

source_registry.citation: AAHA (2023). Senior Care Guidelines — Managing Cognitive Dysfunction and Behavioral Anxiety.
source_registry.use: Senior behavior changes in disorientation, interaction, sleep-wake, house training, activity and anxiety warrant monitoring and veterinary evaluation; early recognition matters.

source_registry.citation: Dog Aging Project environmental/lifestyle data infrastructure (longitudinal companion-dog research).
source_registry.use: Supports longitudinal capture of demographics, behavior, physical activity, environment, diet, medications/preventatives and health context.

source_registry.citation: Social determinants of health and disease in companion dogs — Dog Aging Project cohort.
source_registry.use: Large cohort demonstrates value of combining dog demographics, activity, environment, behavior, diet and health variables.

source_registry.citation: The Science and Social Validity of Companion Animal Welfare (2023).
source_registry.use: Learning, sniffing, play and species-appropriate enrichment can support welfare; recommendations must still be individualized.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Postura corporea abbassata / crouch
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Tronco e/o testa portati più in basso del baseline; possibile riduzione apparente della sagoma.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non equivale da sola a 'ha paura' o 'è sottomesso'.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Irrigidimento / tensione corporea
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Riduzione del movimento fluido, postura rigida, muscolatura apparentemente tesa.
compatible: possibile escalation difensiva se associata ad altri segnali
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non classificare automaticamente come aggressività.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Freeze / immobilità improvvisa
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Interruzione marcata del movimento rispetto ai secondi precedenti.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Il freeze è aspecifico: non è una diagnosi né una previsione certa di morso.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Play bow
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Arti anteriori abbassati con posteriore sollevato, spesso associato a movimenti elastici.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non usare come prova assoluta di stato emotivo positivo se il resto della sequenza è conflittuale.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Approccio volontario
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Riduzione attiva della distanza verso persona/cane/oggetto.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Approccio non significa necessariamente amicizia o comfort.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Allontanamento / evitamento
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Aumento attivo della distanza, spostamento laterale o uscita dal campo rispetto allo stimolo.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non attribuire causa senza conoscere lo stimolo e la sequenza.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Coda bassa o tucked
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Coda tenuta sotto il livello abituale; tucked = tra gli arti posteriori.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: La conformazione di razza e il baseline individuale possono limitare l'interpretazione.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Coda alta
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Coda tenuta sopra il livello abituale del cane.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Coda alta non significa automaticamente dominanza o aggressività.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Tail wag
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Movimento laterale ripetuto della coda; registrare ampiezza, velocità, rigidità e posizione.
compatible: eccitazione positiva o negativa a seconda del contesto
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Scodinzolare non equivale a 'felice'.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Orecchie appiattite / backward
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Padiglioni portati indietro o aderenti rispetto al baseline.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Morfologia delle orecchie e razza modificano la visibilità; segnale non univoco.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Orecchie in avanti
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Padiglioni orientati anteriormente rispetto al baseline.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non equivale da solo a stato positivo o minaccia.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Blink / chiusura occhi
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Chiusura palpebrale breve o prolungata; codificabile come movimento facciale.
compatible: possibile stress se converge con altri segnali
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non attribuire emozione da un singolo blink.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Inner brow raiser / AU101-like
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Sollevamento della parte mediale del sopracciglio, se visibile e compatibile con morfologia.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non usarlo come sinonimo di tristezza, colpa o richiesta.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Lip lick / nose lick
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Lingua che passa su labbra o naso.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: È un segnale altamente aspecifico: mai etichettarlo da solo come stress.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Panting fuori contesto termico/esercizio
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Respirazione a bocca aperta con lingua esposta; annotare se non spiegata da caldo/esercizio.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Senza temperatura, attività e stato clinico non attribuire stress.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Yawning / sbadiglio
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Apertura ampia e temporanea della bocca con pattern tipico di sbadiglio.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Sbadiglio ≠ stress in modo automatico.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Head turn / orientamento via dallo stimolo
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Rotazione della testa o del corpo che riduce l'allineamento con lo stimolo.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non interpretare automaticamente come 'non vuole' senza sequenza e contesto.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Gaze alternation persona-oggetto
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Alternanza ripetuta dello sguardo tra una persona e un target/luogo.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Il target desiderato va inferito solo se la sequenza e la storia personale lo supportano.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Bark event
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Sequenza di abbai; estrarre pitch, durata, intervalli, tonality/noise, repetition rate.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Mai tradurre un abbaio come parola o frase.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Growl event
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Vocalizzazione gutturale a bassa frequenza; registrare bout, durata, pulsazione e contesto.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Growl ≠ aggressione certa; è un segnale contestuale e può comparire nel gioco.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Whine / whimper
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Vocalizzazione più acuta e spesso tonale; annotare durata e ripetizione.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non identificare la causa senza contesto e stato clinico.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Howl / ululato
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Vocalizzazione lunga e sostenuta con struttura tonale.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non assegnare significato unico.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Attenzione umana
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Persona guarda/interagisce/parla al cane oppure è presente ma inattiva.
compatible: modificatore primario di espressioni e comunicazione
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: La stessa azione facciale può cambiare frequenza in funzione dell'attenzione umana.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Interazione cane-cane
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Presenza e comportamento di un conspecifico; distanza, orientamento, reciprocità.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Etichette sociali richiedono sequenza reciproca, non singolo frame.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Risorsa / cibo / toy
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Cibo, ciotola, osso, toy o oggetto di valore nel contesto immediato.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non attribuire 'possessività' senza pattern e interazione.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Separazione / isolamento
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Proprietario esce o cane resta senza referente abituale.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Un singolo episodio non diagnostica ansia da separazione.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Cluster distress/fear
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Convergenza di più segnali: coda tucked, postura abbassata, freeze/escape, tremore, lip lick ripetuto, panting fuori contesto, disengagement.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non diagnosticare disturbo d'ansia; raccomandare aumento distanza e valutazione professionale se persistente/severo.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Cluster possibile escalation difensiva
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Rigidità/freeze + orientamento intenso + growl/snarl/teeth display o avanzamento/ritiro rapido.
compatible: alta tensione con possibile rischio di escalation
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non prevedere morso con certezza. Output deve essere prudente: non avvicinarsi, non testare il cane, aumentare distanza in sicurezza.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Possibile dolore/discomfort
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Cambiamento improvviso di comportamento, postura anomala, vocalizzazioni, ridotta interazione, tensione facciale/orecchie, restlessness o concealment.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Dogly non diagnostica dolore né causa. Se nuovo, intenso o persistente, indirizzare al veterinario.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Consistenza fecale da immagine
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Forma/consistenza visiva stimata in fascia qualitativa; registrare colore apparente e presenza visibile di sangue/muco senza diagnosi.
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Una foto non identifica causa, infezione, parassiti o malattia; lo scoring umano stesso ha variabilità.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Red flags gastrointestinali
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Vomito ripetuto, incapacità di trattenere acqua, sangue evidente, feci nere/catramose, letargia/collasso, addome doloroso o gonfio, segni di disidratazione.
compatible: necessità di contatto veterinario rapido/urgente secondo gravità
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non tentare diagnosi o trattamento farmacologico automatico.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Valutazione nutrizionale contestuale
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Età/life stage, peso/BCS se disponibile, alimento, quantità, snack, cambi dieta, attività e ambiente.
compatible: personalizzazione e correlazione con trend digestivi
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Dogly non prescrive diete terapeutiche o fabbisogni clinici senza supervisione veterinaria.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Razza come prior debole
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Razza o mix dichiarato dall'utente.
compatible: prior leggero su morfologia/visibilità e alcuni tratti di popolazione
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non predire comportamento individuale dalla razza; non usare stereotipi per rischio/aggressività.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Pattern personale
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Stessa configurazione di segnali + contesto ripetuta nello stesso cane con esito/feedback coerente.
compatible: inferenza personalizzata più forte del prior di popolazione
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Non promuovere a pattern dopo singolo evento o solo feedback proprietario.

base_knowledge_cards.label: Astensione obbligatoria
base_knowledge_cards.observable: Video insufficiente, cane non visibile, audio scarso, segnali contraddittori, contesto assente o evidenza bassa.
compatible: output 'non ho abbastanza elementi' + eventuale singola domanda utile
base_knowledge_cards.not_conclude: Mai forzare una traduzione per completare la UX.

life_stage_policy.principle: Use exact age plus an approximate life-stage context. Life stages are context, not deterministic behavior labels.

stages.definition: Birth through cessation of rapid growth; AAHA gives roughly 6-9 months with variation by breed/size.
From end of rapid growth through completion of physical/social maturation; often up to 3-4 years, with individual variation.
After social/physical maturity until the last approximately 25% of estimated lifespan; exact boundary depends on the individual.
Last approximately 25% of estimated lifespan; size/breed/health affect timing, so use as an approximate context.
Insufficient profile data or uncertain stage.

life_stage_policy.implementation_note: Keep current DB age_stage for compatibility. Build a derived LifeStageContext object from birth_date + age_stage + size; include source/confidence. Do not silently rewrite current enum values.

rules: Owner-reported data is context, not objective truth.
System-inferred routine changes require multiple observations or explicit confirmation.
Absence of data must remain UNKNOWN, never imputed as normal.
Prefer deviation from the dog's own baseline over population averages when enough longitudinal data exists.

advice_catalog.action: Increase distance from the trigger and give the dog a real option to disengage; do not force contact.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Observe whether body tension, avoidance or vocalization decreases after distance is increased.

advice_catalog.action: Use a reward-based alternative behavior or redirect; avoid punishment, intimidation or physical correction.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Ask whether the dog can re-engage calmly and whether the unwanted behavior decreases without escalation.

advice_catalog.action: If the dog's health and environment allow it, offer a calm sniffing/exploration opportunity rather than only high-intensity exercise.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Check whether the dog settles more easily afterward compared with its usual baseline.

advice_catalog.action: When today's routine is clearly different from usual, first restore a familiar low-stress routine where practical.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Compare behavior after the routine returns closer to normal.

advice_catalog.action: For a puppy, use gradual positive exposure at a distance where the puppy can stay comfortable; do not force approach.
advice_catalog.follow_up: If fear is intense or persistent, recommend veterinary/behavior professional guidance rather than repeated exposure.

advice_catalog.action: A new or persistent change in sleep, orientation, house training, activity, interaction or anxiety in a senior dog deserves veterinary discussion rather than being attributed to age alone.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Escalate sooner if the change is sudden, severe or accompanied by pain, collapse, breathing difficulty or other red flags.

advice_catalog.action: Record the episode and compare frequency, duration and context with the dog's normal baseline before making a strong conclusion.
advice_catalog.follow_up: Use future repeated observations to decide whether this is a stable personal pattern or a new change.

advice_catalog.action: Do not prescribe fixed exercise minutes from age/breed alone; adapt activity to individual health, temperament, life stage, environment and usual baseline.
advice_catalog.follow_up: If activity advice could be limited by health or mobility, recommend veterinary guidance.

rules: Advice text must come from a closed evidence-backed catalog, not free-form model invention.
The LLM may explain why a catalog item was selected, but may not create a new action or override contraindications.
If safety flags are present, safety policy overrides lifestyle optimization.
Use exact age and life-stage context only as modifiers, never as deterministic explanation.
Prefer the dog's own recent-vs-usual deviation when supported by longitudinal data.
If owner-reported context is the only support, say so internally and keep confidence limited.
Advice outcome feedback is personal learning evidence, not scientific ground truth.

outcome_learning.capture: After an appropriate delay or next related interaction, ask a single low-friction question: 'Ti è sembrato utile?'
personal_learning_rules: Never update scientific KB from one user's outcome.
Personal advice affinity can rise only after repeated comparable episodes.
Do not turn advice success into causal certainty.
Safety/veterinary escalation recommendations are not optimized away by owner feedback.

current_pipeline: backend/app/worker/handlers.py -> observer then reasoner with eligible_memory
backend/app/contracts/interpretation.py -> no scientific-KB evidence source and no advice contract yet
backend/app/contracts/taxonomy.py -> keep current IntentCode allowlist; do not replace it with new research-only intent names
